$comment: Every supported target, keyed by device, region and kernel release. The
files for an entry live at
src/targets/<device>/<region lowercased>/<kernelRelease>/ -- the path is
derived, never written here, so the two cannot drift apart.
'core' names the exploit tree under src/payloads/<payload>/ that this
target's kernel needs, and with it the target-<core>.h in the directory
above and the root-<core>.c glue. The attack chain is fixed to a GKI
branch rather than to a SoC, so a kernel on a different series takes a
different core -- not the same core with different offsets.
This is the hand-authored half of the support feed. Artifact URLs and
sizes are not here: they are only knowable after CI builds them, and
tools/generate_feed.py joins the two into the targets-v2.json the app
reads. See the repository README.
kernelVersion is the complete /proc/version line and kernelBuildVersion is
the '#<n> SMP ...' part of it. `adb shell cat /proc/version` on the device
is the direct way to get them; both are also the kernel's own linux_banner
and UTS_VERSION, so they can be read out of the boot image when no device
is at hand -- that only proves what the image would print, not what the
slot the device actually boots does. A target whose kernelVersion is null
is carried here but left out of the feed, because the app matches on those
exact strings.

targets.status: the first android14-6.1 target, and the first to name core61. The adb route (LD_PRELOAD, non-app build) roots this device end to end on the first attempt in 5 runs out of 7, each started from a boot with at least 9 minutes of uptime (two of the seven were second runs on a boot an earlier run had left alive; counting only first runs it is 4 of 5) -- the other 2 panicked in the sched_setattr punch before the R/W, so a miss costs a ~90 s reboot rather than one of the supervisor's remaining attempts, and the run after one that rooted fails on the per-uid pipe budget its resident helpers still hold: `root install done=1 root=1 uid=2000->2000 su daemon serving` -- the exploit process stays unprivileged on this route by design, that pair is its own uid and `root=1` is the flag saying the helper the kernel exec'd reached uid 0, which the summary line prints as `uid=2000->0` -- and the daemon answers `uid=0(root) ... context=u:r:kernel:s0` -- not the KernelSU that is in this device's init_boot as a debugging aid, which answers u:r:ksu:s0. Every matched field here except kernelVersion is read off the device rather than reasoned from the image, and the offsets come from that device's own boot.img; the bug is unfixed in this image and the waiter shape is the pre-split 0x58 one, both re-checked in the disassembly rather than inherited from the core's other 6.1 targets. Everything the application does after it has a payload is verified too, driven from adb: the release .so loaded through the helper's own --run-payload runner reports both markers the app requires (`exploit completed`, `done=1 root=1`) on the first attempt from a clean boot, the helper stages ksud and `--late-load android14-6.1 me.weishu.kernelsu` answers `KernelSU loaded and answering (0)`, and the manager then shows the LKM Jailbreak-mode card at version 32525-2 with SELinux back to Enforcing, the framework never restarting under any of it (system_server still the pid it took 9.6 s into boot, sixteen minutes and one late-load later) -- this is also the first android14-6.1 KernelSU build in the repository to be loaded anywhere. Only the app's two log markers are checked that way, not the runner exit status its installer also gates on, because the runner is backgrounded so the log can be streamed off before a panic. The application's own route works too, as of core61 leaking the slide through boot_id: two runs from the app on two clean Enforcing boots, first attempt each, uid 10325 in u:r:untrusted_app:s0, reached `done=1 root=1` and the manager then showed the LKM Jailbreak-mode card at 32525-2 with SELinux back to Enforcing and system_server still the pid it took 9.4 s into boot. tracefs is still EACCES from that domain (`slide tracefs setup failed errno=13`); what changed is that it is no longer fatal -- pr_error's exit(-1) was, and the run now falls through to the boot-id source. Two runs are not a rate: the slide adds a second grooming-and-punch stage to a chain whose stages land about two in three, and the app caches the slide per boot so a retry skips that stage. kernelVersion is set from this device's own /proc/version, which puts the target in the feed and its KernelSU build in the job a release waits on. What that has *not* been through is the feed path itself: every run so far read its payload from a folder on the device through the application's debug mode, so the release tag, the asset URLs anchored to it and the size checks will run for the first time when CI publishes this target, as will CI's own build of the app payload and of the android14-6.1 KernelSU pair, which has only ever been built locally. The first feed-served run is the thing to watch The temporary root itself is verified; note that a run leaves SELinux permissive until the next reboot, since nothing on this route puts it back

the first android13-5.15 target, and the first to name core515. Both routes root this build. The standalone route (LD_PRELOAD, non-app) rooted on the first attempt with the slide off tracefs; the application route cannot read tracefs, so it takes the P0 physical oracle, and MediaTek is why that route needed this core's one real divergence from the reference: lk relocates the image's virtual base independently of its physical placement (observed virtual slides 0x12d4600000 through 0x2984400000 against a physical delta that measured zero on every fingerprint), so the oracle places the image physically with the fingerprint and then reads the live misc->fops word off the probe page for the true base -- committing the fingerprint offset as the slide, which is what a Samsung target does, pins the image at its link address and every later address is quietly wrong. That route was verified from the shell over three boots -- one window reject that taught the measured window (KIMAGE_VIRTUAL_BASE_MIN..MAX bounded by vmemmap, not derived by addition), one clean gate miss, one full success (`slide-kaslr-ok source=physical-data virtual_slide=0x2689600000`, `cfi write ret=35`, `root umh result wake=1 complete=1 retval=0 socket=1`, daemon answering uid=0 context=u:r:kernel:s0) -- and then from the app, which reached done=1 root=1 and loaded the KernelSU pair named in kernelsu.json. The slot-0 pipe reclaim loses its race roughly one boot in three, clean and without corrupting anything; SLIDE_ORACLE_ROUND_ATTEMPTS=3 re-runs the round in-attempt the way the reference's fresh-page loop would, while the fops production stage stays single-shot: its miss semantics are unmeasured here, and a dirty miss there is core510's wedged misc_fops, not a retry. kernelVersion is null only because /proc/version has not been captured off the device; everything else matched here was read off the device or its own boot.img. Known, fix staged but not yet through a run: a successful run left its forged references -- the configfs file whose release frees a forged object, and the physrw pipe pair -- with a keeper forked into the caller's domain, and on the application route that keeper is an app-domain process Android reaps within hours of the app going away; its death closed those descriptors and the phone rebooted one to six hours after install, twice. STABILITY_TRANSFER_TO_ROOT hands that set to the resident root helper over the su socket ('h' in hold_refs.c) so nothing in the app's domain holds kernel state, and the keeper remains the fallback for a helper that does not answer the opcode. A run otherwise leaves SELinux permissive between the credential write and ksud's late-load, which reloads policy and restores Enforcing. The bug is unfixed in this image (remove_waiter at image offset 0x01770a90 operating on current, compact 0x58 waiter), and the kernel image is byte-identical to POCO air's on the same build, which is how the symbol offsets were cross-checked

targets.status: the application route is complete here: run from the app under SELinux enforcing it reaches done=1 root=1 and ksud then loads KernelSU -- `late-load: KernelSU loaded and answering (0)`, module Live, enforcing restored -- four times in nine attempts, from a /data/adb this session had emptied first. This is the first target whose KASLR slide does not come from perf_event_open: untrusted_app has no perf_event class, so the slide is taken from the exploit's own write through the `uuid` sysctl entry. kernelVersion and kernelBuildVersion are deliberately empty, which keeps this target out of the feed the app reads, because a feed entry would have CI build its KernelSU from the ddkImage its kernelsu.json names -- and a module built from that generic android12-5.10 DDK reboots this device on load, three runs out of three. The module that works was built from Meta's own source for this build, which the build-kernelsu action cannot fetch. Filling these two fields in is what publishes the target, so they stay empty until the action can take a kernel tree. The manager's Soft restart works here too, which it did not before: Horizon OS starts the zygote through /system/bin/stub_zygote, KernelSU clears the syscall-tracepoint mark on anything init execs that is not /app_process or /adbd, and the zygote that came back from a soft reboot was therefore invisible to every hook -- no setresuid hook fired for any uid afterwards, so the seccomp hole the manager's supercall needs was never punched and its root worker died on syscall 142 with SIGSYS while the module stayed loaded. This build now takes devices/quest3 for it, upstream 953b403a backported onto the pinned 32525. Measured after the fix, on an application-route install: the manager's own Soft restart button brings the framework back with a new zygote that is still marked, no libksud crash in logcat, the module still Live, SELinux still Enforcing, and the manager still showing its LKM Jailbreak-mode card at 32525-2. From a shell-route install, where `ksud debug mark get` can be read, the same soft reboot leaves init, adbd and the new zygote all marked and `su` still answering. Modules survive it too, which they did not before either: a soft reboot leaves the daemons a module started running, and the stage scripts then run a second time against them -- Sui started one more daemon on every soft reboot, and LSPosed, which exits rather than run twice, lost its bridge into the new system_server for good whenever the reboot followed an update, because post-fs-data had replaced the module directory the stale daemon was still sitting in. common/0004 reaps them after `stop` and before the directories are swapped. Measured here, two soft reboots in a row: four leftovers killed, one sui, a fresh lspd reporting version 2.1.1 and `sent service to bridge`, and Zygisk injected into both of the zygote partitions Horizon OS's stub runs
